title: Quinoa vs. Couscous: Nutrition Compared

seo.title: Quinoa vs. Couscous: Nutrition Compared
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g cooked, quinoa has about 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, and 2.8 g fiber; couscous about 112 calories, 3.8 g protein, and 1.4 g fiber.
seo.search_intent: Compare quinoa and couscous for calories, protein, fiber, gluten, and cooking use.

excerpt: Cooked quinoa and couscous are close in calories, but quinoa usually provides slightly more protein and about twice the fiber. Quinoa is naturally gluten-free, while traditional couscous is made from wheat semolina and contains gluten.
content_html:
Quinoa and couscous can occupy exactly the same spot on a plate, but they come from very different foods. Quinoa is a pseudocereal seed; traditional couscous is made from small granules of durum-wheat semolina. That changes gluten, fiber, and some micronutrients far more than it changes calories.

Cooked nutrition per 100 g

QuinoaRefined couscous
Calories~120~112
Protein~4.4 g~3.8 g
Fiber~2.8 g~1.4 g

The calorie gap is only about 8 calories per 100 g. Quinoa has just 0.6 g more protein, but it provides roughly twice the fiber of the refined couscous reference.

At a 180 g serving, that becomes about 5 g fiber from quinoa versus roughly 2.5 g from couscous, which makes the difference easier to see in a real meal.

Gluten is the clearest dividing line

Quinoa is naturally gluten-free. Traditional couscous is made from wheat and contains gluten unless it is a specialty product made from other ingredients.

For someone with celiac disease, that difference matters far more than a fraction of a gram of protein. Processed quinoa products still deserve label checking when strict gluten avoidance is required.

Refining can narrow or widen the nutrition gap

Quinoa generally provides more magnesium and iron than refined couscous. Whole-wheat couscous is different: keeping more of the grain can raise fiber and minerals, so “couscous” is not one fixed nutrition profile.

The fairest comparison is therefore cooked quinoa against the actual couscous product you plan to use, not against an abstract category.

Couscous wins on speed

Many instant couscous products hydrate in only a few minutes. Quinoa usually needs around 15 minutes plus a short rest, but it keeps a firmer, slightly springier texture.

That changes how they fit into meals too: couscous is excellent when you want an almost immediate base, while quinoa tends to hold up well in bowls and make-ahead salads.

Which one should you choose?

If speed matters and gluten is not an issue, couscous is hard to beat. If you want more fiber, a modest protein edge, and a naturally gluten-free base, quinoa has the advantage. Their calorie numbers are too close to be the main reason to choose one over the other.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Cooked quinoa usually has slightly more: about 4.4 g/100 g versus roughly 3.8 g/100 g for couscous.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Quinoa, around 2.8 g/100 g compared with roughly 1.4 g/100 g for refined couscous.

faq.question: Does couscous contain gluten?
faq.answer: Yes. Traditional couscous is made from durum wheat.
